Observed:
- Increasing left leg pain and weakness
- Impaired mobility
- Urinary incontinence
- Elevated inflammatory markers
- Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI
- 87-year-old man with multiple comorbidities
- One week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
- Single episode of urinary incontinence
- Anorexia and 12% body-weight loss over six months
- Low blood pressure responsive to IV fluids
- Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L)
- Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
- Normal cardiac and chest examinations
- Normal abdominal examination
- 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors on neurologic examination
- Mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 on lumbar spine MRI
- No central canal stenosis or abscess on lumbar spine MRI
- Small anterior joint effusion on left hip ultrasound
- Normal tumour markers
- Normal MRI of the hip
- Normal isotope bone scan
- Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI of the hips and pelvis
Differential diagnosis:
1. Idiopathic inflammatory psoas muscle disease
2. Psoas abscess
3. Iliopsoas bursitis
4. Septic arthritis of the hip
5. Polymyalgia rheumatica
